values.note: City of Big Falls: $44.15 a night with electric and water, $31.84 for a primitive site, both including tax and fees. The 7th night of a week's stay is free; monthly rates on request. One RV and one tent, or two tents, per site. Dump station free to registered campers ($10 otherwise). Cancel at least 48 hours ahead for a refund.

values.note: Book on Campspot, or call the city office (218-276-3300) or the camp host (218-556-4825), up to a year ahead. Holiday stays (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day weekends) need 2 nights, paid in full two weeks before arrival. Check-in noon, check-out 11 a.m.

note: City of Big Falls campground among pines near the Bigfork River rapids, with river boat/canoe access and shore fishing; the separate horse camp next door is for horse campers in May, September and October. ATVs may ride into and out of the campground to the multi-use trails; no riding within it. --Claude
summary: City pages, policy PDF and site map read: $44.15 electric+water / $31.84 primitive (tax and fees in), 7th night free, open May to end of October, Campspot or phone booking up to a year ahead, 2-night holiday minimum, showers, dump, WiFi. The stored riverview does not hold up on the city's own site map: every RV site has the loop road and a continuous tree band between it and the river. Pin is on the wrong side of US-71.
flags: WATERFRONT (stored riverview, checked hard): recommend riverview -> not waterfront. The city's rendered site plan (Campground_Site_Plan-Rendered-REDUCED.pdf, scale bar 60 ft) puts the Bigfork River along the NE edge; the sites nearest it, 17, 18 and 19 (about 48.1950,-93.8025 to 48.1952,-93.8029), are 30-45 m from the river's edge with the campground loop road and a continuous tree band drawn between them and the water, matched on imagery (a tree strip along the river bank NE of the loop road). Sites 20-22 (about 48.1955,-93.8040, north of the loop) are about 50+ m from the water behind trees; the open ground by the river is the day-use pavilion area by the restroom/registration building, not a campsite. No source shows the river from any RV site (Campspot type photos unread, no 2027 dates). The old evidence's 'falls visible across open bedrock' was not supported by anything found; under the default-down rule a view needs confirmation, so not waterfront unless a site photo shows the water.

PIN MOVE: stored 48.19430,-93.79950 is EAST of US-71, in trees SE of the bridge, about 259 m from the campground, which is west of the highway (entrance 48.1948,-93.8013; Campspot's own pin 48.194586,-93.801758 is at that entrance). Suggest 48.19505,-93.80280 (between the restroom/registration building and sites 17-19).

ATV wording (operator's own, policy PDF): 'ATVs. ATV's are allowed to drive into and out of the main campground, as long as speed limits are obeyed... No recreational driving throughout the campground... Remember that all area trails are "multi-use" and you must use caution when meeting motorized vehicles.' A town campground that lets ATVs ride in and out to the area's multi-use trails, not an OHV staging area; reviewer to decide (same pattern as Babbitt 5603).

Horse camp: a separate horse-camp area adjoins with its own map; per the policy its sites are 'for horse campers only' May 1-31 and Sept 1-Oct 31 and open to others when the main campground is full. Not a reason to split or drop the main campground.

Phone: stored 218-556-4825 is the camp host cell on the city pages (correct). The city office is 218-276-3300 (also the Campspot number). Website https://bigfalls.govoffice.com/campgrounds answers 200 and is this campground; the Campground Information page above holds the rates.

Sites: the stored note's '32 sites' matches the city site map's numbering 1-32 (with 23 and 24 marked 'UNDEVELOPED SITE', plus a host site), but the page states no count and Campspot's filter shows 'RV Sites 37' / 'All Sites 39' (likely including the horse camp), so sites.count was not written.
